title: Rights follow the role
sub: Film 4 of 7 of From helper to colleague: an agent's rights come from its work, not from a person's. In the 1960s, hospital pharmacists began to fill a drawer for each patient from the doctor's order, instead of leaving every medicine on the ward's shelf. Planning's agent gets its rights the same way: each step of its role says what it reads, writes and calls, and what's left out is another role's step.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's marble and oak; the hospitals of the 1950s and 1960s are painted full-frame, matte and soft-lit, with the place and the years on a tag. Its colours mean the same in every film: blue is tools and structure (the steps, the role and its rights), violet the model thinking, orange data coming back, green a check that passes, and amber a check that fails, or what is left out.
